orchestrator.rationale: Demand is real. The delivery model loses money on every drop at current route density, and a funded national courier entered the Leeds corridor in September. Change pricing and route model before any further capital goes in.
orchestrator.investor: The business has demand and a real customer base. The constraint is structural, so more capital would fund more loss-making routes. Funding should follow a density target, not precede it.
orchestrator.roadmap: Days 0 to 30: reprice and cut sub-threshold routes. Days 30 to 90: sign annual agreements with the top five accounts. Day 90: re-audit. Move to PROCEED when density holds at 14 stops or more for eight weeks.

findings.title: The segment is crowded
findings.text: At least four funded players sell a similar offer to the same buyers in Cardiff.

findings.title: Addressable market is smaller than claimed
findings.text: The market sizing counts adjacent segments that the product does not serve today.

findings.title: Core offer is easy to replicate
findings.text: The description names no feature that a larger player could not build within two quarters.

findings.title: Burn outpaces revenue growth
findings.text: Monthly burn grew faster than revenue over the last two quarters.

findings.title: Runway is short
findings.text: Cash at the current burn lasts less than twelve months.

findings.title: Gross margin is thin
findings.text: Gross margin sits below the range seen in comparable businesses.

findings.title: Delivery rests on one person
findings.text: A single founder holds the critical supplier and customer relationships.

findings.title: Single supplier dependency
findings.text: One supplier provides a component with no tested alternative.

findings.title: Processes will not scale
findings.text: Core operations are manual and will not hold at twice the volume.

findings.title: A funded entrant can undercut on price
findings.text: A competitor with recent funding announced a lower-priced offer for the same buyers.

findings.title: An incumbent could bundle the feature
findings.text: The leading platform in the category could add this as a feature for existing customers.

findings.title: Price pressure is likely
findings.text: Two competitors cut prices in the last quarter.

findings.title: Buyers do not yet trust the brand
findings.text: Interviews show buyers prefer an established name for this purchase.

findings.title: Buyers are price-sensitive
findings.text: Buyers ranked price first when service levels were similar.

findings.title: Existing habits are hard to change
findings.text: The product asks buyers to change a routine they are comfortable with.

findings.title: Social proof is thin
